analysis: Examined LaunchAgent.swift (base and head) and the StartupPreloader.swift patch. LaunchAgent change: adds ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP) to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (head lines 282-283, 294). It flows through passthroughEnvironment (head 325-346) into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables only when the value is non-empty. Same allowlisted, non-secret rollback-knob pattern as existing keys. No new argv, no change to the worker key handling (head 333-337), no change to the stop/disable lifecycle, and no widening of the plist trust surface (TB-003/T-013 unchanged). StartupPreloader patch: adds an optional shapeWarmup closure run after a load and after a passing self-test, or directly after load when no self-test is configured. Per the patch, warmup is not called when a self-test fails (the failure path retires or continues) and cancellation breaks the loop. Security-relevant observations: the warmup is excluded/non-serving, takes only a model ID, and returns Void. It does not interact with the E2E-encrypted prompt path (A-001), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), attestation, or authorization (TB-011). Residual questions outside the supplied evidence: the patch excerpt for StartupPreloader is truncated, so the catch/fail-closed branches after line ~198 were not visible. The warmup implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy and the caller wiring) is not in the supplied files. Integration should confirm that warmup input is synthetic, does not populate or donate to the prefix cache with attacker-influenced or tenant data, does not delay registration or grant application beyond acceptable bounds, and does not run for a retired model. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
